title: Evaluating AI agents for marketing campaign automation | Hightouch

facts.fact: According to McKinsey research cited by Hightouch, agentic AI could potentially automate 60% of all marketing tasks.
facts.quote: According to [recent McKinsey research](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/our-insights/reinventing-marketing-workflows-with-agentic-ai), agentic AI could potentially automate 60% of all marketing tasks.

facts.fact: Hightouch cites Stanford's 2026 AI Index accuracy benchmarks, which tested 26 top-tier frontier models and found hallucination rates ranging from 22% to 94%.
facts.quote: Across 26 top-tier frontier models tested in [Stanford's latest accuracy benchmarks](https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report/responsible-ai), hallucination rates range wildly from 22% to 94%.

facts.fact: Hightouch states that a baseline failure rate of at least 22% applies to ungoverned AI agents, a figure it draws from the Stanford hallucination range.
facts.quote: A baseline failure rate of 22% (at minimum) for ungoverned AI agents is disastrous for brand campaigns.

facts.fact: Hightouch's article identifies three failure modes that it says appear consistently across agentic marketing deployments.
facts.quote: Three failure modes appear consistently across agentic marketing deployments.

facts.fact: The Hightouch article was published on March 2, 2026, by author Alex McPeak.
